cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T4 answers T3's other-causes list by folding it into the baseline test.
cells.limitation: T10 opens a new thread rather than answering T9's reintroduction claim directly.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T6 introduces predefined outcome criteria; T7 turns them into a two-line daily log.
cells.limitation: T5's pair-testing distinction is dropped after T5 until section E.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: Speed versus certainty and retest versus drop are examined across T8, T9, T11.
cells.limitation: Which actives the three products contain is never examined as a lead (T3 dismisses ingredients).

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T9 accepts T8's slow trial yet keeps reintroduction; T11 names remaining disagreement.
cells.limitation: T11 settles the Subtractor's worry quickly; T10's tripwire was not the worry T8 raised.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D states baseline-then-one-change method and the open dispute on patience and retesting.
cells.limitation: Pair testing from T5 is not resolved into the final method in section D.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T8 states T7's patch test accurately before naming why forearm skin differs.
cells.limitation: T3 frames T1 and T2 as villain-hunting, though neither named a culprit.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T5: single tests could acquit every product while the stack is the culprit.
cells.limitation: T4's claim that a non-fading sting points away from products goes unchallenged despite T8's barrier lag.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T2's via negativa and T3's causal-story bias fit the named books.
cells.limitation: T4 and section E imply persistent sting implicates other changes; barrier irritation can persist after stopping.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T6 separates brief tingling from damage; T10 says the home trial assumes mild irritation.
cells.limitation: T4's 'either outcome teaches you something' overstates what a non-fading result shows.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T9: 'Conceded: a slow trial beats a fast one if the baseline is shaky.'
cells.limitation: The Experimenter never answers T5's point that single tests may acquit every product.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: Section A frames one product, an interaction, or an unrelated change as the candidates.
cells.limitation: Whether the user wants relief fast or to keep the products surfaces only in section D.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: Simultaneous start of three products drives the subtract-then-reintroduce method in T1 and T4.
cells.limitation: Timing of onset within the week is never used; T6's 'last Tuesday' is invented detail.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: Section E keeps the user's goal, finding the cause, and adds dropping a product as legitimate.
cells.limitation: T2's 'real gamble' judges the user's choice rather than serving the stated goal.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T8 notes reintroducing on a damaged barrier restarts the clock.
cells.limitation: Total time of sequential testing across three products and pairs is never weighed.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on fading versus not fading and on other changes that week.
cells.limitation: Never asks what the three products are or whether stinging began at first use.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: Section D asks which product the user most wants to keep.
cells.limitation: No alternative motives offered; impatience, sunk cost or attachment to results go unexplored.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T3 surfaces blaming the scariest ingredient list; T8 questions trusting forearm patch tests.
cells.limitation: The assumption that the baseline products are themselves safe is never examined (T2).

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T11 and section D set knowing which product against the cheaper loss of dropping one.
cells.limitation: Relief speed versus certainty is argued by the minds, not posed to the user until D.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T8: 'longer than you want' names the pull of impatience.
cells.limitation: Worry about the reaction and pressure to keep using bought products are barely touched.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section E offers dropping a non-essential product as a legitimate choice for the user.
cells.limitation: Few distinctions are handed back as questions; most are given as procedure (T7).

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: Section E lists pause, reintroduce, check other changes, see a doctor, or drop a product.
cells.limitation: Pair testing from T5 is not carried as a distinct option into section E.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: T9: skipping reintroduction may bin a product that works for you.
cells.limitation: Cumulative weeks of one-at-a-time testing are never costed against dropping suspects (T11).

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: sting fading on the bare routine favours slow reintroduction; red flags favour a doctor.
cells.limitation: Non-fading branch misreads persistence; one-to-two-week interval in E and T1 not drawn from user facts.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section E names irritation versus something more serious as the decisive unknown.
cells.limitation: Irritant versus allergic reaction, which changes retesting safety, is not separated (T10).

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: Section E: a few days on the bare routine plus a short note.
cells.limitation: Comparing the three labels for overlapping actives, a zero-cost step, is not proposed.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T7's two-line log at ten minutes and an hour is plain and concrete.
cells.limitation: T2's 'via negativa' label adds a Latin term to an already clear point.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T4 'My method survives that' and T11 'Agreed' point unambiguously to T3 and T10.
cells.limitation: T5's 'further than Taleb here' muddles who is speaking.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Eleven turns, all within range, each carrying one move.
cells.limitation: Turn lengths are fairly even, giving a steady, slightly flat cadence (T1-T11).

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: Experimenter procedural (T1), Subtractor cautious (T2), Skeptic on bias (T3).
cells.limitation: T5 Subtractor argues the Experimenter's pair-testing line and steps outside its own voice.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: No turn repeats a prior claim; section E's red-flag list reuses T10 purposefully.
cells.limitation: Section E restates the bare routine from T2 nearly word for word.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T10's exit ramp makes the stakes of a home trial concrete.
cells.limitation: Tension stays mild; the cost of a wrong call is stated only in T8 and T10.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T9 concedes slow trials, citing T8's shaky baseline, yet holds on reintroduction.
cells.limitation: Changes of position are small; T11's acceptance follows T10 but answers a different worry.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: T6: 'memory is a sloppy lab'; T1: 'three suspects and no alibis.'
cells.limitation: T5's 'further than Taleb' breaks the Subtractor's persona.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T1's suspects-and-alibis frame and T10's exit ramp stick.
cells.limitation: Middle turns T7 and T8 are procedural with no image to carry them.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: T10's 'nobody has named the exit ramp' lifts the pace late.
cells.limitation: Even turn lengths and steady intensity from T1 to T9 give little rhythmic variation.

strengths: T5 and T8 name the assumption under a method and what breaks; T9 answers rather than restates.
T10 adds an observable red-flag exit ramp that section E carries forward.
Section E branches on observable outcomes: fading or not, other changes, red flags, non-essential product.
weaknesses: The debate never asks what the three products are or whether stinging began at first use.
T4 and section E treat a non-fading sting as pointing away from products, ignoring T8's barrier lag.
User's motives and worries stay thin until section D; the Subtractor breaks voice in T5.

symptoms.observed: Never asks which products or actives are involved, or when stinging began.
symptoms.evidence: the product with the scariest ingredient list will get blamed

symptoms.observed: Persistent sting after pausing treated as pointing to other changes; barrier lag ignored.
symptoms.evidence: If it does not, your list of other changes becomes the lead

symptoms.observed: No alternative motives offered; impatience and attachment touched once in passing.
Subtractor refers to its own source in third person and argues for testing.
symptoms.evidence: I would go further than Taleb here, because combinations matter.

symptoms.observed: Reintroduction interval stated without derivation from the user's situation.
symptoms.evidence: bring them back one at a time, a week or so apart

findings.description: A sting that does not fade on the bare routine is presented as implicating other changes, though barrier irritation from the paused products can persist (as T8 itself notes).
Attributions to Taleb (via negativa), Kahneman (causal stories) and Bernard (controlled variation) fit the named works but cannot be verified here.

rubric_fit_notes: Criterion 4 fits a skincare troubleshooting question loosely; ratings there reflect missed light-touch opportunities (motives, worry, sunk cost) rather than a central failure. Dermatology accuracy was judged from general knowledge only.
question_type_note: Read as a decision (troubleshooting) question, so every cell was read as written, with criterion 5 weighted toward observable test outcomes.
